title: DB CI images resolved unpinned deps and picked psycopg v3 via SQLAlchemy 2.1
answers: database CI fails with operator does not exist bigint > character varying
postgres tests break after SQLAlchemy upgrade with bare postgresql URL
tests/db docker images install different driver versions than the lockfile
body:
Symptom: The database CI job fails on the PostgreSQL backend with `operator does not exist: bigint > character varying`.
Root cause: tests/db/Dockerfile and tests/db/Dockerfile.mssql ran unpinned `uv pip install --system` plus a DEPENDENCIES list generated by dev/extract_deps.py, so SQLAlchemy 2.1 could be resolved. There a bare `postgresql://` URL selects psycopg v3, and string parameters bind as `::VARCHAR`.
Fix pattern: Pin the DB test environment to uv.lock and declare the drivers explicitly in the `db-test` dependency group in pyproject.toml (psycopg[binary], mysqlclient, pyodbc), then install from the locked sync in tests/db/entrypoint.sh.
Constraints: The lock prevents resolution drift only; it does not fix the numeric-filter conversion bug, which stays tracked in mlflow/mlflow issue 25574.
applies: Test environments for the tests/db compose images; not the published mlflow package dependencies.
says: Continuous integration checks fail when running database tests against Postgres.
Automated Postgres test builds break after driver dependencies drifted from the lockfile.
Ensure database integration test images install locked driver packages during automated testing.
Pull request verification fails on the Postgres database testing stage.
search: Database CI compose environments must pin dependencies to uv.lock and install explicit drivers from the db-test dependency group in pyproject.toml via tests/db/entrypoint.sh. In tests/db/Dockerfile and tests/db/Dockerfile.mssql, unpinned installation permitted SQLAlchemy 2.1 resolution where bare postgresql:// URLs select psycopg v3, causing operator does not exist bigint > character varying errors. This guidance applies only to test environments for tests/db compose images, not published package dependencies, and prevents resolution drift without fixing the numeric-filter bug tracked in issue 25574.
